{"id":"mimid-1wgh.37.90.7","title":"wg: targeted-messages-01 L68 The draft defines a new wire format but never says how support for it...","description":"draft-ietf-mls-targeted-messages (targeted-messages-01), Format / IANA Considerations (MLS Wire Formats). Editors' copy mlswg/mls-targeted-messages at ae3ab52, L68.

Text: "This document defines the `mls_targeted_message` WireFormat, where the content
is a `TargetedMessage`."

Problem: The draft defines a new wire format but never says how support for it is signalled or checked. RFC 9420 Capabilities has no wire-format field, and extensions-10 Section 5 adds supported_wire_formats and required_wire_formats for exactly this; its changelog says targeted-message support is signalled that way. Without a rule, a sender cannot know whether the recipient can process the message, and a recipient that cannot will drop it silently.

Suggested fix: Normatively reference draft-ietf-mls-extensions. Require that a sender MUST NOT send a TargetedMessage to a member whose LeafNode does not list mls_targeted_message in supported_wire_formats, unless the GroupContext's required_wire_formats includes it.

Severity: medium. Verifier: keep (Confirmed. extensions-10 lines 872-875 say Capabilities lacks wire formats and define supported_wire_formats and required_wire_formats. Its changelog (lines 1986-1987) says targeted-message support is "now signaled using support_wire_formats and required_wire_formats". The draft has no normative references besides RFC 9420 and 9180, and says nothing about signalling. No existing issue covers this (#4, #5 and #6 are unrelated).)
